title: Don't Give up your Seat
theme: A life entrusted to us, a place to cherish, and a promise beyond this world
opening: We spend our lives navigating responsibilities, disappointments, and circumstances beyond our control. But what if, in the midst of it all, we're overlooking something far more precious than anything this world can offer?
prayer: Heavenly Father,  Thank You for the gift of my life and the place You have given me in Your creation.  When worldly concerns consume my thoughts, remind me of what truly matters. Give me the strength to fulfill my responsibilities without losing sight of You.  Teach me to cherish each day, especially when life becomes difficult, and to recognize Your presence in both my joys and my struggles.  May I never take for granted the life You have entrusted to me, and may every day bring me closer to You.  Amen.
body:
In today's Gospel, the Pharisees attempt to trap Jesus with a question about paying taxes to Caesar. They flatter Him with words of admiration, yet their intentions are anything but sincere.

Jesus, knowing their hearts, simply responds:

“Then repay to Caesar what belongs to Caesar and to God what belongs to God.” — Matthew 22:21

How extraordinary that such a simple answer carries such profound truth.

Jesus does not dismiss our earthly responsibilities. He acknowledges them while reminding us that God's authority is above all.

And it made me think about our human lives.

I imagine God's creation as a great theater, where each of us has been given a seat. That seat is our human life, a precious opportunity to know God, to love, to serve, and to journey toward eternal life.

Yet how easily we become consumed by the performance around us. Our worries, ambitions, disappointments, conflicts, and desire for control can become so overwhelming that we forget the gift of simply being here.

We begin to believe that the events unfolding before us are everything.

But they are not.

Our earthly circumstances are temporary. Our relationship with God reaches toward eternity.

To cherish our seat does not mean life will be without suffering. It means recognizing that even through suffering, our life remains a gift worthy of love, gratitude, and care.

We are called to fulfill our responsibilities in this world, but never to allow the world to become greater than the One who created it.

Perhaps that is what Jesus is reminding us.

Give the world what is rightfully owed, but never surrender to it what belongs to God.

And what belongs to God?

Our very lives.

We have each been given a seat in God's creation—a human life through which we can come to know Him and journey toward eternity. Whatever unfolds around us, let us never forget the value of the place we've been given. Cherish it. Protect it. Don't give up your seat.
